blocks.text:
After breakfast, you will set off for the equator. The first stop is Mitad del Mundo. The complex commemorates the geodetic expedition of 1736. A 30-metre monument was built here between 1979 and 1982, with a symbolic equator line marked on the ground. GPS later showed that the actual line lies about 240 m further north.

You will then visit the Intiñan Museum. Here, water experiments and egg-balancing demonstrations accompany explanations about the equator and the cultures of the region. The displays include totems, traditional houses and everyday objects.

The next stop is the Pululahua Geobotanical Reserve. This vast volcanic crater is still inhabited, with small local farms on its floor. The land is worked by hand or with oxen, growing maize and beans. The reserve also includes forested slopes and a deep river canyon. Pululahua combines geology with everyday life: from the upper viewpoint, you can see fields, roads and individual houses inside the caldera. Described as one of the largest inhabited craters, it is especially interesting for anyone fascinated by volcanism. Changes in altitude and humidity make the vegetation on its slopes much denser than in the open highlands visited on previous days.

After taking photographs at the viewpoint, transfer to El Crater 4*. The afternoon is free. Meals: breakfast.
